criteria.justification: The operation uses only `addReview(productId: $productId, rating: $rating, body: $body)` with selections `id`, `rating`, `body`, and `product { id }` — no invented fields like `reviewText`/`title`, no rating enum, and no update/delete mutations.
The mutation body invokes the field exactly as `addReview(productId: ..., rating: ..., body: ...)`.
The operation declares `$productId: ID!` and passes it as `addReview(productId: $productId, ...)`.
Declared as `$rating: Int!` and typed as `rating: number` in TypeScript, passed as the literal `5`.
`$body: String` is nullable, the TS parameter is `body?: string`, and it is coerced with `body: body ?? null`.
The selection set contains only `id`, `rating`, `body`, and `product { id }`, all of which exist on Review.
The request is issued through the client with `{ authenticated: true }`, routing it via the authenticated request path.
